verses.text: These are the wise sayings of Solomon. Solomon was the son of David, and Solomon was king of Israel.
Wise Lessons for Life will help you learn to be wise, to accept correction, and to understand wise sayings.
Wise Lessons for Life will teach you to develop your mind in the right way. You will learn to do what is right and to be honest and fair
Wise Lessons for Life teach people who know very little to be wise. They will teach young people what they need to know and how to use what they have learned
A wise person will listen and gain more learning. A person with understanding will get good guidance.
These Wise Lessons for Life will help you understand wise sayings and what they mean, the words of wise people, and the hidden meaning behind their sayings.
Respecting the LORD is where knowledge begins. But foolish people look down on wisdom and discipline.
Son, listen to your father's instruction, and do not abandon your mother's teaching.
Your father's instruction and your mother's teaching will be like a beautiful wreath on your head, like a fine necklace around your neck.
My son, if sinners try to lure you into sin, do not go along with them.
If they say: Come with us, let us hide and wait to attack someone and spill blood. Let us hide and ambush an innocent person for no reason.
Let us swallow them alive, like the grave swallows people. Let us swallow them whole, like those who go down into the pit.
We will find all kinds of valuable things, and we will fill our houses with what we have taken.
Join us and share what we get. We will all share one moneybag together.
My son, do not walk in the same path with them. Keep your feet away from their path.
Their feet run to do evil, and they hurry to spill blood.
It is useless to spread a net where a bird can see it.
But these men hide and wait to ambush their own blood. They hide to attack their own lives.
This is what happens to everyone who is greedy for unfair gain. It takes away the life of the person who has it.
Wisdom calls out loudly in the street. Wisdom raises her voice in the public square.
Wisdom cries out at the noisy street corners, at the entrance of the city gates. Wisdom says:
How long will you simple people love being simple? How long will mockers enjoy mocking, and fools hate knowledge?
Turn and listen when I correct you. I will pour out my thoughts to you. I will make my words known to you.
I called you, but you refused to listen. I reached out my hand, but no one paid attention.
You ignored all my advice, and you did not want my correction.
So I will laugh when trouble comes to you. I will make fun of you when terror strikes you —
when terror comes on you like a storm, and trouble comes on you like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
Then they will call out to me, but I will not answer. They will look for me, but they will not find me.
This is because they hated knowledge, and they did not choose to respect the LORD.
They did not want my advice, and they rejected all my correction.
So they will eat the fruit of the way they chose to live, and they will be filled with the results of their own plans.
The simple people will be killed because they turn away, and foolish people will be destroyed because they feel safe and satisfied.
But whoever listens to me will live safely and will be at peace, without fear of harm.

1.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by nouns and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs. Verses 6-33, previously missing, have been added (verses 6-9 using wording supplied directly by the pastor), completing this chapter.

verses.text: My son, if you accept my words and treasure my commands within you,
So that you pay close attention to wisdom and set your heart on understanding,
If you call out for insight and raise your voice for understanding,
If you search for it like silver and look for it like hidden treasure,
Then you will understand what it means to respect the LORD, and you will find the knowledge of God.
Because the LORD gives wisdom; knowledge and understanding come from the LORD's mouth.
The LORD stores up sound wisdom for honest people. The LORD is a shield for those who live with integrity.
The LORD guards the paths of justice and protects the way of his faithful people.
Then you will understand what is right, fair, and honest — every good path.
When wisdom enters your heart, and knowledge is pleasant to you,
Good judgment will protect you, and understanding will keep you safe.
Wisdom will save you from the way of evil people, from those who say twisted, dishonest things,
From people who have left the right paths to walk in dark ways,
Who enjoy doing evil and take pleasure in the twisted ways of wicked people,
Whose paths are crooked and whose ways are dishonest.
Wisdom will also save you from another man's wife, from a woman who is unfaithful and flatters you with smooth words,
Who has left the husband of her youth and forgotten the promise she made before God.
Her house leads down to death, and her paths lead to the dead.
No one who goes to her ever comes back; they never find the path of life again.
So walk in the way of good people, and stay on the paths of the righteous.
Honest people will live in the land, and people of integrity will remain in it.
But wicked people will be cut off from the land, and those who betray it will be pulled out by the roots.

2.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by nouns (e.g. 'He layeth up' -> 'The LORD stores up') and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: My son, do not forget my teaching. Let your heart keep my commands,
because they will add many years to your life, and bring you peace.
Do not let mercy and truth leave you. Tie them around your neck; write them on your heart.
Then you will find favor and a good name in the sight of God and people.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not depend on your own understanding.
In all your ways, honor the LORD, and the LORD will make your paths straight.
Do not think you are wise in your own eyes. Respect the LORD, and turn away from evil.
This will bring health to your body and refreshment to your bones.
Honor the LORD with your wealth, and with the first and best part of everything you produce,
then your barns will be filled to overflowing, and your wine barrels will overflow with new wine.
My son, do not reject the LORD's discipline, and do not be tired of the LORD's correction,
because the LORD corrects the one the LORD loves, just as a father corrects the son he delights in.
Happy is the person who finds wisdom, the person who gains understanding.
Wisdom is worth more than silver and brings a better profit than fine gold.
Wisdom is more precious than rubies. Nothing you desire can compare with her.
Long life is in her right hand; riches and honor are in her left hand.
Her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.
She is a tree of life to those who hold on to her, and happy is everyone who keeps her close.
By wisdom the LORD laid the foundations of the earth; by understanding the LORD set the heavens in place.
By the LORD's knowledge the deep waters were divided, and the clouds drop down dew.
My son, do not let sound wisdom and good judgment out of your sight; hold on to them,
and they will be life for your soul and a graceful ornament around your neck.
Then you will walk on your way safely, and your foot will not stumble.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid; you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
Do not be afraid of sudden terror, or of the trouble that comes on wicked people, when it comes,
because the LORD will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being caught in a trap.
Do not hold back good from people who deserve it, when it is in your power to help them.
Do not say to your neighbor, Go away and come back, I will give it to you tomorrow, when you already have it with you.
Do not make plans to hurt your neighbor, because your neighbor lives near you and trusts you.
Do not start an argument for no reason with someone who has done you no harm.
Do not envy a violent person, and do not choose to live like they do,
because the LORD hates a dishonest person, but the LORD is close with honest people.
The LORD's curse is on the house of wicked people, but the LORD blesses the home of honest people.
The LORD mocks those who mock others, but the LORD gives favor to humble people.
Wise people will inherit honor, but fools will be promoted to shame.

3.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with pronouns replaced by nouns (e.g. 'he shall direct thy paths' -> 'the LORD will make your paths straight'), each verse capitalized, and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: Listen, my children, to a father's instruction. Pay attention, so that you may gain understanding.
Because I am giving you good teaching. Do not turn away from my instruction.
When I was a boy in my father's house, still tender and my mother's only child,
my father taught me and said: Let your heart hold on to my words; keep my commands, and you will live.
Get wisdom, get understanding. Do not forget it, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.
Do not turn away from wisdom, and wisdom will protect you. Love wisdom, and wisdom will watch over you.
Wisdom is the most important thing, so get wisdom. Whatever else you get, get understanding.
Treasure wisdom highly, and wisdom will lift you up. Wisdom will bring you honor when you embrace her.
Wisdom will place a graceful garland on your head; wisdom will give you a beautiful crown.
Listen, my son, and accept what I say, and the years of your life will be many.
I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have led you on straight paths.
When you walk, your steps will not be held back, and when you run, you will not stumble.
Hold on tightly to instruction. Do not let it go. Guard it well, because it is your life.
Do not enter the path of wicked people, and do not walk in the way of evil people.
Avoid it. Do not travel on it. Turn away from it and go on.
Because wicked people cannot sleep until they do something wrong; they cannot rest until they make someone fall.
They eat food that comes from wickedness, and they drink wine that comes from violence.
But the path of honest people is like the light of dawn, growing brighter and brighter until it is full daylight.
The way of wicked people is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble.
My son, pay attention to my words. Turn your ear to what I say.
Do not let my words out of your sight. Keep them deep in your heart,
because they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.
Guard your heart more than anything else, because your life flows from it.
Get rid of dishonest talk, and keep lying lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and fix your gaze on what is in front of you.
Think carefully about where your feet are going, and all your ways will be secure.
Do not turn to the right or to the left. Keep your foot away from evil.

4.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with each verse capitalized and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: My son, pay attention to my wisdom, and turn your ear to my understanding,
So that you may keep good judgment, and your lips may guard knowledge.
Because the lips of another man's wife drip sweetness like honey, and her mouth is smoother than oil,
But in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to the grave.
She does not think about the path of life. Her ways wander, and she does not even know it.
So now, my children, listen to me, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.
Keep your path far away from her, and do not go near the door of her house,
So that you do not give your honor to others, or your years to someone cruel,
So that strangers do not grow rich from your wealth, and what you worked for does not end up in a stranger's house,
And at the end of your life you groan, when your body and flesh are worn out,
And you say: How I hated instruction! How my heart looked down on correction!
I did not listen to my teachers or turn my ear to those who instructed me.
I was soon in complete ruin in front of the whole community.
Drink water from your own well, running water from your own spring.
Should your springs flow out into the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?
Let them belong to you alone, and not to strangers along with you.
Let your fountain be blessed, and find joy in the wife of your youth,
A loving deer, a graceful doe. Let her love satisfy you always; be captivated always by her love.
Why, my son, would you be captivated by another man's wife, and embrace a woman who is not your own?
Because a person's ways are in full view of the LORD, and the LORD examines all their paths.
The sins of a wicked person will be a trap; the wicked person will be held fast by the ropes of their own sin.
The wicked person will die for lack of discipline, and be led astray by their own great foolishness.

5.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with each verse capitalized and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs. Verse 5's 'hell' was corrected to 'the grave,' since the Hebrew word here is sheol (the realm of the dead), not the New Testament concept of hell (gehenna).

verses.text: My son, if you have promised to pay someone else's debt, if you shook hands to guarantee a stranger's loan,
You have trapped yourself with your own words; you are caught by what you said.
So do this now, my son, to free yourself, since you have fallen into your neighbor's hands: Go and humble yourself; press your case with your neighbor.
Do not let your eyes sleep, and do not let your eyelids grow heavy.
Free yourself, like a deer from a hunter's hand, like a bird from a trapper's hand.
Go watch the ant, you lazy person. Consider its ways and become wise.
The ant has no commander, no overseer, no ruler,
Yet it stores up its food in the summer and gathers its supplies at harvest.
How long will you lie there, you lazy person? When will you get up from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
And poverty will come on you like a robber, and need like an armed man.
A worthless and wicked person goes around saying dishonest things,
Winking with his eyes, signaling with his feet, pointing with his fingers,
With twisted plans in his heart, always scheming evil, always stirring up conflict.
So disaster will strike him suddenly; he will be broken instantly, beyond healing.
There are six things the LORD hates, seven things that are disgusting to the LORD:
Proud eyes, a lying tongue, hands that kill innocent people,
A heart that plans wicked schemes, feet that run quickly to do evil,
A false witness who lies, and someone who stirs up conflict among family members.
My son, keep your father's command, and do not abandon your mother's teaching.
Tie them on your heart always; fasten them around your neck.
When you walk, they will guide you. When you sleep, they will watch over you. When you wake up, they will speak with you.
Because the command is a lamp, and the teaching is a light, and correction from instruction is the way to life,
To keep you from an evil woman, from the smooth talk of a woman who is unfaithful.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her eyes capture you.
Because a prostitute can be had for the price of a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts for your very life.
Can a man carry fire against his chest without burning his clothes?
Can someone walk on hot coals without burning his feet?
So it is with the man who sleeps with his neighbor's wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
People do not look down on a thief who steals food because he is starving,
But if he is caught, he must pay back seven times as much; he must give up everything he owns.
But a man who commits adultery with a woman has no sense at all. Whoever does it destroys himself.
He will be wounded and disgraced, and his shame will never be erased.
Because jealousy makes a husband furious, and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge.
He will not accept any payment; he will refuse to be satisfied no matter how large the gift.

6.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with each verse capitalized and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs.

verses.text: My son, keep my words, and store up my commands within you.
Keep my commands and live; guard my teaching like the apple of your eye.
Tie them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom: You are my sister, and call understanding your close relative,
So that they will keep you from another man's wife, from a woman who is unfaithful and flatters you with her words.
One day I looked out through the window of my house, through the lattice,
And I saw among the simple people, I noticed among the young men, a young man who had no sense.
He was walking down the street near her corner, going the way to her house,
At twilight, as the day was fading, in the dark of night.
Just then a woman came out to meet him, dressed like a prostitute, with a crafty heart.
She was loud and rebellious; her feet did not stay at home.
One moment she was in the street, the next in the public square, lurking at every corner.
She grabbed him and kissed him, and with a shameless face she said to him:
I had to offer a peace offering today, and I have paid what I promised.
So I came out to meet you; I looked for you, and I have found you!
I have covered my bed with colorful blankets, with fine linen from Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let us drink deeply of love until morning; let us enjoy ourselves with love,
Because my husband is not home; he has gone on a long journey.
He took a bag of money with him and will not come home until the day of the full moon.
With her persuasive words she led him astray; with her smooth talk she convinced him.
He followed her at once, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a criminal being led away in chains to be punished,
Until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird rushing into a snare, not knowing it will cost him his life.
So now, my sons, listen to me; pay attention to what I say.
Do not let your heart turn to her ways; do not wander onto her paths,
Because she has brought down many wounded; she has killed a mighty crowd of men.
Her house is the road to the grave, leading down to the chambers of death.

7.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with each verse capitalized and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs. V22's obscure 'as a fool to the correction of the stocks' has been rendered as 'like a criminal being led away in chains to be punished,' matching the natural Hebrew word order noted by scholars (fetters/restraints for correcting a fool). V27's 'hell' was rendered 'the grave' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with the same fix in chapter 5.

verses.text: Is not wisdom calling out? Is not understanding raising her voice?
She stands at the top of the hills, beside the road, where the paths meet.
She cries out beside the gates, at the entrance of the city, at the doorways:
To you, people, I call out; my voice speaks to all humanity.
You who are simple, learn to be wise. You who are foolish, gain understanding.
Listen, because I will speak excellent things; when I open my lips, I will say what is right.
My mouth will speak the truth, and my lips hate wickedness.
All the words of my mouth are honest; none of them are twisted or dishonest.
They are all clear to someone who understands, and right to those who find knowledge.
Choose my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge instead of the finest gold.
Because wisdom is worth more than rubies, and nothing you could want compares to it.
I, wisdom, live together with good judgment; I have found knowledge and careful thinking.
To respect the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, evil ways, and dishonest talk.
Good advice and sound wisdom belong to me; I have understanding, I have strength.
Kings rule by me, and rulers make just laws.
By me princes govern, and nobles, all who judge fairly on the earth.
I love those who love me, and those who search for me early will find me.
Riches and honor are with me, lasting wealth and what is right.
My fruit is better than gold, better than the finest gold, and what I produce is better than choice silver.
I walk in the way of what is right, along the paths of justice,
Giving wealth to those who love me, and filling their treasuries.
The LORD had me at the very beginning, before the LORD's earliest works, long ago.
I was appointed from eternity, from the very beginning, before the earth even existed.
I was born before the oceans, before the springs filled with water.
Before the mountains were set in place, before the hills, I was born,
Before the LORD had made the earth or its fields, or the very first dust of the world.
When the LORD set the heavens in place, I was there. When the LORD drew the horizon on the face of the deep,
When the LORD set the clouds above, when the LORD made the springs of the deep sea strong,
When the LORD gave the sea its boundary so that the waters would not go past what the LORD commanded, when the LORD marked out the foundations of the earth,
I was right there beside the LORD, like a skilled craftsman. I was the LORD's daily delight, always rejoicing in the LORD's presence,
Rejoicing in the LORD's whole world, delighting in the human race.
So now, my children, listen to me. Happy are those who keep my ways.
Listen to instruction and become wise; do not turn away from it.
Happy is the person who listens to me, watching at my doors every day, waiting beside my doorway.
Because whoever finds me finds life, and receives favor from the LORD.
But whoever fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every 'he/his' referring to the LORD replaced by 'the LORD' explicitly (vv22-31), and each verse capitalized to match the rest of the book. V30's debated Hebrew word 'amon' is rendered 'like a skilled craftsman,' one of the two major scholarly traditions for this word (the other being 'little child').

verses.text: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out its seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat; she has mixed her wine; she has also set her table.
She has sent out her servant girls; she calls out from the highest points of the city:
Whoever is simple, let them come in here! To those who lack sense, she says:
Come, eat my food, and drink the wine that I have mixed.
Leave your simple ways and live; walk in the way of understanding.
Whoever corrects a mocker will be insulted; whoever rebukes a wicked person will be hurt.
Do not rebuke a mocker, or the mocker will hate you. Rebuke a wise person, and the wise person will love you.
Give instruction to a wise person, and the wise person will become even wiser. Teach a righteous person, and the righteous person will learn even more.
Respecting the LORD is where wisdom begins, and knowing the Holy One is understanding.
Because through wisdom your days will be many, and years will be added to your life.
If you are wise, your wisdom will reward you. If you mock, you alone will suffer for it.
The woman named Foolishness is loud; she is simple and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat at the highest point of the city,
Calling out to those who pass by, who are going straight on their way:
Whoever is simple, let them come in here! To those who lack sense, she says:
Stolen water is sweet, and food eaten in secret tastes good.
But the simple person does not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of the grave.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with each verse capitalized and vocabulary chosen to match natural ASL signs. V18's 'hell' rendered 'the grave' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with earlier chapters.

verses.text: These are the proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son brings sorrow to his mother.
Treasures gained by wickedness do not profit anyone, but doing what is right saves you from death.
The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but the LORD refuses to satisfy the desires of the wicked.
Lazy hands make a person poor, but hard-working hands bring wealth.
Whoever gathers crops in summer is a wise child, but whoever sleeps during harvest is a child who brings shame.
Blessings crown the head of the righteous, but violence fills the mouth of the wicked.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot away.
The wise in heart accept commands, but a foolish chatterer will fall.
Whoever walks with integrity walks safely, but whoever twists their ways will be found out.
Whoever winks slyly causes trouble, and a foolish chatterer will fall.
The mouth of a righteous person is a fountain of life, but violence fills the mouth of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up conflict, but love covers over every wrong.
Wisdom is found on the lips of someone with understanding, but a rod is for the back of someone with no sense.
Wise people store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool invites disaster.
The wealth of the rich is their strong city; the poverty of the poor is their ruin.
What the righteous earn leads to life; what the wicked gain leads to sin.
Whoever accepts correction is on the path to life, but whoever ignores correction leads others astray.
Whoever hides hatred with lying lips, and whoever spreads slander, is a fool.
Too many words always lead to sin, but whoever controls their lips is wise.
The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth very little.
The lips of the righteous nourish many, but fools die for lack of sense.
The LORD's blessing makes a person rich, and the LORD adds no trouble along with it.
A fool finds pleasure in doing wrong, but a person with understanding finds pleasure in wisdom.
What the wicked fear will happen to them, but what the righteous desire will be granted.
When a storm sweeps through, the wicked are gone, but the righteous stand firm forever.
As vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is a lazy person to those who send him on an errand.
Respecting the LORD adds years to your life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
The hope of the righteous brings joy, but the expectation of the wicked comes to nothing.
The way of the LORD is a stronghold for honest people, but it brings ruin to those who do wrong.
The righteous will never be uprooted, but the wicked will not remain in the land.
The mouth of the righteous produces wisdom, but a dishonest tongue will be cut out.
The lips of the righteous know what is right to say, but the mouth of the wicked speaks only dishonesty.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter shifts style to short two-line proverb couplets; generic 'he' pronouns rendered as gender-neutral 'whoever/someone who' throughout.

verses.text: The LORD hates dishonest scales, but accurate weights please the LORD.
When pride comes, shame follows, but wisdom is with the humble.
The honesty of honest people guides those honest people, but the crookedness of dishonest people destroys those dishonest people.
Riches do not help on the day of judgment, but doing what is right saves you from death.
The righteousness of a blameless person makes their path straight, but the wicked fall because of their own wickedness.
The righteousness of honest people saves them, but dishonest people are trapped by their own greed.
When a wicked person dies, their hope dies with them; everything they expected from their power comes to nothing.
The righteous person is rescued from trouble, and it falls on the wicked instead.
With their mouth, a godless person destroys their neighbor, but righteous people are saved through knowledge.
When the righteous succeed, the city celebrates; when the wicked die, there is shouting for joy.
Through the blessing of honest people, a city is built up, but through the mouth of the wicked, it is torn down.
Whoever has no sense looks down on their neighbor, but someone with understanding stays quiet.
A gossip goes around revealing secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
Where there is no guidance, a nation falls, but many advisers bring safety.
Whoever promises to pay a stranger's debt will suffer for it, but whoever refuses to guarantee a debt is safe.
A kind woman gains respect, and ruthless men gain only riches.
A merciful person helps himself, but a cruel person brings trouble on himself.
A wicked person earns deceptive wages, but whoever plants righteousness reaps a true reward.
Righteousness leads to life, but whoever chases after evil chases after death.
The LORD hates those with twisted hearts, but the LORD delights in those whose ways are honest.
Be sure of this: the wicked will not go unpunished, but those who are righteous will be kept safe.
Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman with no sense.
What the righteous want leads only to good; what the wicked expect leads to anger.
One person gives freely and yet grows richer; another withholds more than is right, and it leads only to poverty.
A generous person will prosper; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.
People curse the one who hoards grain, but blessing crowns the one who sells it.
Whoever searches for good finds favor, but whoever looks for trouble finds it.
Whoever trusts in their riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like a green leaf.
Whoever brings trouble on their own family inherits only wind, and a fool becomes a servant to someone wise.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and whoever wins souls is wise.
If the righteous are repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with generic 'he' pronouns rendered gender-neutral throughout.

verses.text: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is foolish.
A good person receives favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns someone with wicked schemes.
No one can be made secure through wickedness, but the root of the righteous cannot be moved.
A worthy wife is a crown for her husband, but a shameful wife is like rot in his bones.
The thoughts of the righteous are honest, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
The words of the wicked lie in wait to shed blood, but the mouth of an honest person is a rescue.
The wicked are overthrown and are gone, but the house of the righteous stands firm.
A wise person is praised, but a twisted mind is despised.
Better to be a nobody with a servant than to act important and have no food.
A righteous person cares for the life of their animal, but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel.
Whoever works the land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases worthless ideas has no sense.
The wicked crave what evil people have gained, but the root of the righteous produces fruit.
The wicked are trapped by their own sinful talk, but the righteous escape from trouble.
A person is satisfied with good things from the words of their mouth, and the work of their hands is repaid to them.
The way of a fool seems right to that fool, but whoever listens to advice is wise.
A fool's anger shows itself at once, but a sensible person overlooks an insult.
Whoever speaks the truth reveals what is right, but a false witness reveals deceit.
Reckless words cut like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
Truthful lips last forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
Deceit fills the hearts of those who plan evil, but joy fills those who work for peace.
No harm comes to the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
The LORD hates lying lips, but the LORD delights in those who deal honestly.
A sensible person keeps knowledge to themselves, but a fool's heart blurts out foolishness.
Hard-working hands will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
Worry weighs down the heart, but a kind word cheers it up.
The righteous give good direction to their neighbor, but the way of the wicked leads others astray.
A lazy person does not even roast the game they caught, but a hard worker's possessions are valuable.
In the way of righteousness there is life, and along that path there is no death.

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with generic 'he' pronouns rendered gender-neutral throughout.

verses.text: A wise child listens to a father's instruction, but a mocker does not listen to correction.
From the fruit of their words a person enjoys good things, but the desire of the treacherous is for violence.
Whoever guards their mouth protects their life, but whoever talks too much comes to ruin.
The lazy person craves things and gets nothing, but the diligent person's desires are fully satisfied.
A righteous person hates lying, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Righteousness guards the person of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
Some pretend to be rich but have nothing; some pretend to be poor but have great wealth.
A person's riches may ransom their life, but a poor person hears no threats.
The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
Pride only leads to conflict, but wisdom is found in those who take advice.
Wealth gained dishonestly disappears quickly, but whoever gathers wealth little by little makes it grow.
Hope delayed makes the heart sick, but a wish fulfilled is like a tree of life.
Whoever scorns instruction will pay for it, but whoever respects a command will be rewarded.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
Good sense wins favor, but the way of the treacherous is hard.
Every sensible person acts with knowledge, but a fool displays foolishness.
A wicked messenger brings trouble, but a trustworthy envoy brings healing.
Poverty and shame come to whoever ignores instruction, but whoever accepts correction will be honored.
A desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools hate to turn away from evil.
Whoever walks with the wise grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
Trouble follows sinners, but good rewards the righteous.
A good person leaves an inheritance for their grandchildren, but the wealth of sinners is stored up for the righteous.
A poor person's field may yield much food, but injustice sweeps it away.
Whoever spares the rod hates their child, but whoever loves their child is careful to discipline them.
The righteous eat until they are fully satisfied, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with generic 'he' pronouns rendered gender-neutral throughout.

verses.text: Every wise woman builds up her house, but a foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.
Whoever walks with integrity respects the LORD, but whoever is devious in their ways despises the LORD.
A fool's talk brings a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the feeding trough is empty, but a strong ox brings a large harvest.
A truthful witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
A mocker looks for wisdom and never finds it, but knowledge comes easily to someone with understanding.
Stay away from a fool, because you will not find knowledge on their lips.
The wisdom of a sensible person is to understand their own way, but the foolishness of fools is deception.
Fools mock at making things right, but goodwill is found among the honest.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of honest people will flourish.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
A faithless person will be paid back for their own ways, and a good person will be rewarded for theirs.
The simple believe anything, but a sensible person watches their step.
A wise person is careful and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
A quick-tempered person acts foolishly, and a schemer is hated.
The simple inherit foolishness, but the sensible are crowned with knowledge.
Evil people will bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
The poor are disliked even by their own neighbors, but the rich have many friends.
Whoever looks down on their neighbor sins, but blessed is whoever is kind to the poor.
Don't those who plan evil go astray? But those who plan good find love and faithfulness.
All hard work brings profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the foolishness of fools stays foolish.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a deceitful witness pours out lies.
Respecting the LORD is a strong fortress, and it gives their children a place of safety.
Respecting the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
A large population is a king's glory, but without people a ruler is ruined.
Whoever is patient has great understanding, but whoever is quick-tempered displays foolishness.
A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.
Whoever oppresses the poor insults their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God.
The wicked are brought down by their own wrongdoing, but the righteous have a refuge even in death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of someone with understanding, and even among fools she becomes known.
Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
A king favors a wise servant, but his anger falls on one who brings shame.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with generic 'he' pronouns rendered gender-neutral throughout.

verses.text: A gentle answer turns away anger, but harsh words stir up wrath.
The tongue of the wise uses knowledge well, but the mouth of fools pours out foolishness.
The eyes of the LORD are everywhere, watching over both the evil and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, but a deceitful tongue crushes the spirit.
A fool despises a father's instruction, but whoever accepts correction is sensible.
In the house of the righteous there is great treasure, but the earnings of the wicked bring trouble.
The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but the hearts of fools are not so honest.
The LORD hates the sacrifice of the wicked, but the LORD delights in the prayer of honest people.
The LORD hates the way of the wicked, but the LORD loves whoever pursues righteousness.
Strict discipline awaits whoever leaves the right path; whoever hates correction will die.
The grave and the place of destruction lie open before the LORD; how much more, then, the hearts of people!
A mocker does not like being corrected, and will not seek advice from the wise.
A happy heart makes a cheerful face, but heartache crushes the spirit.
The heart of someone with understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.
All the days of the oppressed are hard, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
Better a little with respect for the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
Better a meal of vegetables where there is love than a fattened calf with hatred.
A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but whoever is patient calms a dispute.
The way of the lazy person is blocked with thorns, but the path of honest people is a highway.
A wise child brings joy to a father, but a foolish person despises their mother.
Foolishness brings joy to someone with no sense, but a person with understanding walks a straight path.
Plans fail without good advice, but they succeed with many advisers.
A person finds joy in giving a good answer, and how good is a word spoken at just the right time!
For the wise, the path of life leads upward, turning them away from the grave below.
The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but the LORD protects the widow's boundaries.
The LORD hates the thoughts of the wicked, but pure words are pleasing to the LORD.
Whoever is greedy for gain brings trouble on their own family, but whoever hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous thinks carefully before answering, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked, but the LORD hears the prayer of the righteous.
A cheerful look brings joy to the heart, and good news gives strength to the body.
Whoever listens to life-giving correction will be at home among the wise.
Whoever ignores discipline despises themselves, but whoever accepts correction gains understanding.
Respecting the LORD teaches wisdom, and humility comes before honor.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. V11 and v24's 'hell' rendered 'the grave' / 'the grave below' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with earlier chapters.

verses.text: A person can plan their thoughts, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.
All a person's ways seem right in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.
Commit your work to the LORD, and your plans will succeed.
The LORD has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of trouble.
The LORD hates everyone who is proud in heart; be sure of this: they will not go unpunished.
Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for; through respecting the LORD a person turns away from evil.
When a person's ways please the LORD, the LORD makes even their enemies live at peace with them.
Better a little with righteousness than great income with injustice.
A person's heart plans their path, but the LORD directs their steps.
The king speaks with divine authority; his mouth must not betray justice.
Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are the LORD's work.
Kings hate wrongdoing, because a throne is made secure through righteousness.
Honest lips please kings; they value someone who speaks the truth.
A king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise person will calm it.
When a king's face lights up, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
How much better to get wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is better than silver!
The highway of honest people avoids evil; whoever watches their step protects their life.
Pride goes before destruction, and a proud spirit before a fall.
Better to be humble with the poor than to share plunder with the proud.
Whoever handles a matter wisely finds success, and blessed is whoever trusts in the LORD.
The wise in heart are called understanding, and pleasant words make instruction persuasive.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who have it, but instruction is wasted on fools.
The heart of the wise makes their words wise, and their lips become more persuasive.
Pleasant words are like a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
A worker's appetite works for them; their hunger drives them on.
A worthless person digs up evil, and their words are like a scorching fire.
A dishonest person spreads conflict, and a gossip separates close friends.
A violent person lures their neighbor and leads them down a path that is not good.
Whoever narrows their eyes is plotting dishonesty; whoever purses their lips is bent on evil.
Gray hair is a crown of glory, found in the way of righteousness.
Better to be patient than powerful, and better to control your temper than to capture a city.
The dice may be thrown into the lap, but the LORD alone decides the outcome.

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with 'the LORD' named explicitly throughout and no vague 'that person' phrasing.

verses.text: Better to be poor and honest than to be a liar and a fool.
It is not good for a person to be without knowledge. If you hurry and do something too quickly, you will make mistakes.
People destroy their lives when they do foolish things, then they get angry and blame the Lord and say it is his fault.
When someone is rich, they have a lot of friends, but if he becomes poor, he has no friends.
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will not escape.
Everyone wants to be friends with an important person. They also want to be friends with someone who gives away gifts.
A poor man's brothers do not like him, and his friends will avoid him even more. When he really needs them, they stay away from him. There is no one there to help him.
To obtain wisdom is to love yourself; those who do what they have learn shall do good
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will not escape.
It is not normal for a fool to be rich or for a slave to rule over princes!
A wise man does not become angry quickly. He always wants to forgive the mistakes of other people.
The shouts of an angry king are like a roaring lion, but his kind words are like the dew on the grass.
A foolish child brings a lot of trouble to his father and a complaining wife is like the constant dripping of water.
People receive houses and money from their parents, but a good wise wife is a gift from the LORD.
A lazy people wants to sleep all day, and someone who will not work will not have any food to eat.
People who obey the commandments of the LORD will live. But he that ignores God’s ways shall die.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will reward them for what they have done.
Discipline your children while there is still hope. Avoiding it because of their crying will end badly for them.
A person who gets angry quickly will always have trouble. If you help him, you will have to help him again and again.
If you listen to what people teach you and you learn from them, you will have wisdom in the end.
People make a lot of plans about what they want to do, but the advice of the LORD will endure.
The most important thing that you want from other people is for them to kind. It is better to be poor than to be a liar.
The fear the LORD and you will have a good life, one that is satisfying and protected during trouble.
A lazy man puts his hand in the bowl to take food, but he is too lazy to bring back his hand to his mouth.
If you punish a mocker, the simpleminded will learn a lesson; if you correct the wise, they will be all the wiser.
Children who would steal from their father and chase away their mother are a child that causes shame and bring disappointment.
My son, if you stop learning, you will turn your back on knowledge.
Using a criminal as a witness makes a joke of justice. Sinful people love to do things that are wrong.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and stripes for the back of fools.

19.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Fixed several typos and grammar issues.

verses.text: Wine is deceiving, and alcohol causes fighting; everyone led astray by them lacks wisdom.
People should be afraid of an angry king, like they are of a lion that roars. If you make the king angry, you can lose your life.
It is an honor for people to stop from strife: Any fool can start an argument.
Because of the cold a lazy person will not prepare their fields: then in the summer they shall beg for food, and no one shall give to them.
Getting information from someone can be like getting water from a deep well. If you are wise, you can draw it out.
There are many people who say: ‘You can trust me.’ But there are only a few of them that do what they promise.
Good people live in the right way and are honest. God blesses their children who live like they do.
When a king sits on his throne to judge people, he separates out all evil with his eyes.
No one can say, I have made my heart clean, have never done anything sinful.
The LORD hates people that use the wrong weights and measures to cheat others.
Even children show what they are like by the things they do. You can see if their actions are pure and right.
The Lord has given some people ears to hear and some people eyes to see.
Do not love excessive sleep, or you will become poor; Open your eyes so that you can do your work and you will be satisfied with bread.
When a person is buying something, they always say, “It's no good. It costs too much.” Then they go away and tell others what a good deal they got.
There is gold, and an abundance of jewels; But the words of someone who is wise are even more precious.
Take the garment of anyone who puts up collateral for a stranger; hold it in pledge if he does it for an unfamiliar woman.
If you have cheated someone to get food, it will taste good in the beginning but in the end, The guilt and consequence will be bitter.
Get good advice before you make your plans. Before you start a war, ask for the advice of wise advisors.
A gossip goes around telling secrets. Don’t be friends with someone who does not care what he says.
Those who would curse their father or mother are like a lamp that goes out in the darkest night.
If someone gets money that he inherited too quickly, when he is too young, It will not be a blessing in the end.
Don’t say, “I will get even for this wrong.” Wait for the LORD to handle the matter.
The Lord hates people who cheat when they weigh things and who are dishonest
No person knows what will happen to him. It is the Lord who decides what will happen to us.
Think carefully before you promise to give something to God. Later, you might wish you had not made that promise.
A king who is wise can find out who is guilty and punish those who have done wrong.
The LORD gave us our mind and conscience; we cannot hide our thoughts and doings from Him.
Mercy and truth protect a king, and his throne is made secure by mercy.
We admire a young man for his strength, but we respect an old man for his gray hair.
Sometimes it takes a painful experience to make us change our ways.

20.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Fixed several typos, a duplicated phrase (v9), and a garbled verse (v28) that had drifted from the actual meaning of the Hebrew.

verses.text: These are the wise sayings that King Lemuel’s mother taught him:
My child, I am your mother. I prayed to God and He gave you to me.
Don't waste your strength or your life on women. Do not give your efforts to things that destroy kings.
Lemuel, kings should not drink wine, Or for rulers to desire strong drink.
If they drink too much, they will not remember the laws and will not be able to judge the people in trouble rightly.
Alcohol is for the dying, and wine for those of bitter of heart
Let them drink and forget their troubles. Let them forget about all their suffering.
Speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves. Help people who are in trouble.
Speak for them and be fair when you judge, and protect the people who can not help themselves and who have nothing.
A wife of honest character is hard to find. She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trust her. He will never have to steal because he is poor
She does good for her husband all her life, and she never brings him trouble.
She gets wool and flax and enjoys making things with her hands.
She is like the merchants' ships; she brings her food from far away.
She gets up while it is dark and she prepares food for her family and for the servants who work for her.
She looks carefully at a field and buys it and she plants the vineyard
Her arms are strong, and she keeps on working.
When she sees people wanting to buy the things that she makes, she works all night.
She makes thread with her hands, and she weaves at the loom and makes clothes.
She loves giving to poor people and those who can not protect themselves and who have nothing.
She does not worry about her family when it snows because they all have warm clothes.
She makes blankets and her clothes are made of linen and purple wool.
Everyone knows her husband. He sits with the leaders of the land at the gate.
She makes clothes and sells them, and she gives the merchants sashes to sell.
She is a strong and a neat woman, and people honour her. She is not worried about what will happen.
She always speaks words of wisdom, and she teaches her people to be friendly.
She oversees the care of her house. She is never lazy.
Her children respect and praise her, and her husband says she is a good wife. He says:
'There are a lot of good women, but you are better than all of them.'
A woman does not always stay young and beautiful, but you should always praise a woman who serves and fears the Lord.
She must get the reward for her hard work, and everyone in the city must praise her.

31.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Merged-verse numbering bugs (16/17/18, 27/28) have been split apart, and archaic leftover phrasing modernized.
